record.original_question: For 0 < beta < 1, let M_beta be the one-dimensional centered fractional maximal operator and let q = 1/(1-beta). Is the derivative map f -> (M_beta f)' both bounded and continuous from W^{1,1}(R) to L^q(R)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $0<\beta<1$ and set $q=1/(1-\beta)$. For $f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{R})$, define the one-dimensional centered Hardy–Littlewood fractional maximal function by
$$M_\beta f(x)=\sup_{r>0}\frac{1}{(2r)^{1-\beta}}\int_{x-r}^{x+r}|f(y)|\,dy,\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}.$$
Let $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the Sobolev space of integrable functions whose distributional derivative belongs to $L^1(\mathbb{R})$, equipped with the norm $\|f\|_{W^{1,1}}=\|f\|_{L^1}+\|f'\|_{L^1}$.

Determine whether the map
$$f\longmapsto (M_\beta f)'$$
is both bounded and continuous as a map from $W^{1,1}(\mathbb{R})$ into $L^q(\mathbb{R})$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has resolved analogous questions for the (non-fractional) one-dimensional centered Hardy–Littlewood maximal operator, proving continuity of f↦(Mf)' from W^{1,1}(R) to L^1(R), and for the uncentered fractional case in higher dimensions. For the centered fractional case in one dimension with 0<β<1 and q=1/(1−β), boundedness of the derivative map is conjectural; partial results show that boundedness would imply continuity, but the full boundedness/continuity statement does not appear to have been established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Continuity for the one-dimensional centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator at the derivative level
status_evidence.snippet: Proves the continuity of the map f↦(Mf)' from W^{1,1}(R) to L^1(R) for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator (β=0 case).
status_evidence.claim: The β=0 analogue is solved, but the fractional case 0<β<1 is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: On the continuity of maximal operators of convolution type at the derivative level
status_evidence.snippet: Continuity at the derivative level for centered convolution-type maximal operators; for the centered fractional maximal operator in d=1, conjectured boundedness implies continuity.
status_evidence.claim: The full boundedness/continuity for the centered fractional case in 1D remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: Endpoint Sobolev continuity of the fractional maximal function in higher dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes endpoint Sobolev continuity in the uncentered fractional setting in higher dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Related but distinct setting; centered 1D fractional case left open.
